title: Irreversibility and Heat Generation in the Computing Process
venue: IBM Journal of Research and Development, 1961
supports: Establishes that erasing a bit dissipates at least kT ln 2, the reason a reversible substrate is interesting at all; the paper's framing of 'information is not destroyed' in the audited repositories descends from this.

title: Logical Reversibility of Computation
venue: IBM Journal of Research and Development, 1973
supports: Shows computation can be made logically reversible, so the bit-exact reversal audited here is not a curiosity but a known design goal.

title: Reversible computing
supports: Introduces reversible cellular automata as a computing substrate; the Margolus/BBM rule audited here is an instance of this programme.

title: Conservative logic
supports: Conservative logic: a primitive whose transitions preserve a conserved quantity. Used to state precisely what the billiard-ball block rule conserves (Hamming weight) and what the topological lock claims to conserve (Euler characteristic).

title: Physics-like models of computation
supports: Physics-like models of computation: the partitioned block scheme with alternating offsets, which is exactly the two-phase structure the audited implementation uses.

title: Cellular Automata Machines
supports: Reference treatment of reversible block cellular automata and the billiard-ball model; the 16-state block permutation table audited here is the textbook construction.

title: Molecular dynamics of a classical lattice gas: Transport properties and time correlation functions
supports: The HPP lattice gas the second laboratory implements: four boolean channels, head-on collision, streaming. Also the origin of the known limitations of the model that the paper uses to interpret the measured forces.

title: Lattice-Gas Automata for the Navier-Stokes Equation
supports: Lattice-gas automata reproducing the Navier-Stokes equation: the reference point for what a lattice gas must reproduce if a measured force is to be called hydrodynamic rather than a fluctuation.

title: Cellular automaton fluids 1: Basic theory
supports: Basic theory of cellular-automaton fluids, including the statistical care needed before a lattice simulation's macroscopic claim is accepted.

title: Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines
supports: The rejection-sampling scheme that the topological-charge laboratory implements: an invariant that is conserved by rejecting every move that would change it is a definition, not a measurement.

title: Digital topology: Introduction and survey
venue: Computer Vision, Graphics, and Image Processing, 1989
supports: Digital topology survey: what the Euler characteristic does and does not determine about a binary lattice, used to argue that the conserved chi is a checksum of the picture rather than a memory of its shape.

title: [1806.07366] Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
supports: Neural ODEs: the continuous-time adjoint used to train with O(1) activation memory, the same trade the audited symplectic network makes in discrete time.

title: Evaluating Derivatives
venue: Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics, 2008
supports: Reference on algorithmic differentiation, including checkpointing and the memory/time trade-off curve against which an O(1)-activation method should be placed.

title: Why Most Published Research Findings Are False
supports: Why most published research findings are false: the statistical frame for treating a single-seed positive result as a hypothesis rather than a finding.

title: Estimating the reproducibility of psychological science
supports: Large-scale replication study; the template for reporting a claim-by-claim reproduction verdict instead of an overall impression.

title: Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research
supports: Ten simple rules for reproducible computational research; rule-level justification for shipping the experiment plan, the pinned subject commit and the raw logs with the paper.

title: 1,500 scientists lift the lid on reproducibility
supports: Survey of reproducibility practice across fields; motivates the audit format (what was re-run, what was not, and why).

title: The ASA Statement on p -Values: Context, Process, and Purpose
supports: The ASA statement on p-values: the reason the paper reports a mean, a standard error and its ratio to zero instead of a dichotomous significance verdict.

title: The preregistration revolution
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2018
supports: The preregistration argument, transposed here to experiment plans fixed before the numbers are read.

title: An Introduction to the Bootstrap
supports: Bootstrap and resampling reference for the interval reporting used when a metric is not normally distributed.

title: GitHub - kostyk348/timelock-ca · GitHub
supports: The audited artifact itself: the repository whose four laboratories, printed verdicts and README claims are the subject of this paper. Cited as an artifact, not as an authority.

title: Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons
supports: Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons: the sense in which a topological invariant stores a logical state and protects it locally, against which the audited Euler-characteristic lock is being contrasted.

title: Topological quantum memory
supports: Topological quantum memory: the error model and threshold argument that make an invariant a memory rather than a checksum; the reference point for saying the audited lock is the latter.
